- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged decline — reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.
- When true outcome shows early sharp drop (e.g., first 3–5 days), model often fails to recognize it — shift forecast downward by 2–5% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to drift toward historical mean — apply mean reversion correction with 1–3% downward bias for next 7–14 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period volatility — increase forecast by 1–2% for days 20–30 if sentiment is neutral or positive.
